summary: Yahweh sends Nathan to David: there were two men in one city one rich many flocks herds, one poor one little ewe lamb bought nourished grew with him and children ate of his morsel drank of his cup lay in bosom as daughter, traveler came to rich man who spared own flock but took poor man's ewe lamb and prepared for traveler. David's anger burns against man must pay fourfold and die. Nathan says you are the man, thus says Yahweh I anointed king, delivered from Saul, gave master's house wives, gave house of Israel and Judah, if too little would add more, why despised word of Yahweh doing evil in eyes, struck Uriah Hittite with sword of Ammonites, taken his wife. Therefore sword shall not depart from your house, I will raise evil against you from own house, you did secretly I will do before all Israel. David says I have sinned against Yahweh, Nathan says Yahweh has put away your sin you shall not die, but because deed made enemies blaspheme child born shall die. Nathan goes house, Yahweh strikes child sick, David fasts lies on ground seven days, elders try raise, child dies, David arises washes anoints changes clothes goes to house Yahweh worships, then house eats, servants puzzled why fasted while alive but rise when dead, David says while child alive I fasted who knows Yahweh may be gracious child may live, now dead why fast, I shall go to him but he will not return to me. Then comforts Bathsheba goes bears Solomon Jedidiah beloved of Yahweh. Joab fights Rabbah sends for David to take city lest be called by my name.
whyItMatters: Nathan's parable is model confrontation — story that makes David condemn himself, then 'you are the man.' Shows sin's consequences despite forgiveness, and pattern of repentance.

keyVerses.text: Nathan said to David, “You are the man! This is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.
David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against Yahweh.” Nathan said to David, “Yahweh also has put away your sin. You will not die.
keyVerses.why: Confession and assurance — sin put away you shall not die.

keyVerses.text: But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”
keyVerses.why: Grief with hope — I shall go to him.

questions.question: How does Nathan's parable work as confrontation?
questions.answer: Nathan doesn't accuse directly but tells story: rich with many flocks, poor with one little ewe lamb bought nourished like daughter, traveler comes rich spares own flock takes poor's lamb. David's anger burns, says man who did shall die and pay fourfold — applies law for theft of sheep (Ex 22:1 fourfold). David judges self — his sentence reveals his own crime: as king with many wives he took Uriah's one wife. Nathan then says you are the man — you are rich man. Brilliant prophetic method: get self-condemnation before revelation. Then recounts grace: I anointed, delivered from Saul, gave master's house wives, house Israel Judah, if too little would add more — why despised word? Shows sin not from lack but contempt.

questions.question: Why does Nathan say sword shall not depart from house, I will raise evil from own house, you did secretly before all Israel?
questions.answer: Consequence oracle: because David struck Uriah with sword of Ammonites (used Ammonites), sword shall not depart — i.e., violence will continue in family: Amnon kills, Absalom kills Amnon, Absalom rebels. You did secretly, I will do before all Israel and sun — refers to Absalom lying with fathers concubines publicly on roof where David saw Bathsheba. Shows sin's pattern repeats and is exposed. Not that God causes evil but that consequences of David's model — taking what not his, secrecy, power abuse — will be lived out by sons.

questions.question: What does David's response 'I have sinned against Yahweh' and Nathan's 'Yahweh put away your sin you shall not die but child shall die' mean about forgiveness and consequence?
questions.answer: David's confession brief after Psalm 51's longer version — I have sinned. Nathan says Yahweh has put away (transferred, taken away) sin you shall not die — death penalty for adultery and murder under law (Lev 20:10, 24:17) but forgiven, life spared. Yet because deed made enemies of Yahweh blaspheme (gave occasion), child born shall die. Shows distinction between forgiveness (relationship restored, death penalty remitted) and consequences remain (child death, sword not depart). Not that child punished for David's sin as guilt transfer, but consequence of David's world disorder. David's later grief response shows trust: child alive fasted who knows gracious, dead why fast I shall go to him but he will not return — hope of reunion, early hint of afterlife.
